passage:
"Papa! Papa!"
"One minute, Vidya, I'm on a call."
"PAPA!" A spoon clattered to the floor, then a cup.
"Vidya, no throwing." Pranav closed the laptop and sat down beside her. "You tapped my arm before and I did not turn. That was my miss. You are cross."
She sniffed. "Pa-pa. Look."
"Yes! Thank you for asking with words. I'm looking. What do you want to show me?"
She held up a wet sock.

qa.q: What did Vidya throw when she was not noticed?
qa.a: A spoon clattered to the floor, then a cup.

qa.q: Why did Vidya scream and throw things instead of waiting?
qa.a: She wanted her father's attention and had already been overlooked, so even an angry reaction was better than none.

qa.q: How did Pranav respond so that calm asking was rewarded and not only the storm?
qa.a: He set aside the laptop, named her feeling, owned that he had missed her tap, and thanked her for saying "Pa-pa. Look." 🙂

qa.q: How does Pranav's call look from Vidya's point of view?
qa.a: To her it is simply a time when Papa is not looking at her. She cannot yet wait or tell a call from being ignored.

grounding: A toddler tantrums for notice because angry attention beats none; the parent answers the need calmly and praises calm asking.

passage:
Monday. Aparna was on the phone. Sunaina, two, screamed and threw her bowl. Aparna shouted back, then gave her full attention.

Wednesday. Sunaina tugged her sleeve softly. "Mumma, play?" Aparna put the phone down. "You asked so nicely! Yes."

Two weeks later. Sunaina wanted attention. She tapped Aparna's knee. "Mumma?" Aparna smiled. "Thank you for asking. I'm listening."

qa.q: What did Sunaina throw on Monday?
Why did Sunaina scream and throw her bowl?
qa.a: Sunaina felt frustrated and ignored, and wanted attention, even angry attention.

qa.q: What changed Sunaina's way of asking?
qa.a: Aparna began praising and responding to calm asking, instead of only noticing the tantrums.

qa.q: How might Aparna feel two weeks later?
qa.a: Aparna likely feels relieved and proud that Sunaina now asks gently.

grounding: Shows a toddler tantrumming to be noticed, and a parent learning to meet the need calmly and praise calm asking.

passage:
In the Hyderabad flat, Nirmala was cooking and chatting to her sister. Noor, two, tugged her dupatta. No answer. Noor threw her spoon and screamed.

Nirmala turned off the stove, knelt and said calmly, "You wanted me. Next time, say 'Ammi.'"

"Ammi," Noor said.

"Good asking! Come, help me stir." She lifted Noor onto her hip.

qa.q: What was Noor feeling when she threw her spoon and screamed?
qa.a: Noor felt frustrated and left out, wanting her mother to notice her.
Nirmala calmly met Noor's need, taught her to say "Ammi," and praised her for asking calmly.

qa.q: How might Nirmala's sister see the scene?
qa.a: The sister might see Noor as naughty, but Nirmala shows that Noor simply needed attention.

grounding: Shows a toddler tantrumming for attention and a parent who responds to the need calmly and praises calm asking.
